prompt: What should I look for in a mobile detailer?
engine: Gemini (gemini.google.com, logged out, site storage cleared before the prompt)
answer:
Gemini said

When hiring a mobile car detailer, convenience is a major perk, but you want to make sure you aren't sacrificing quality, safety, or accountability. Because the mobile detailing industry has a low barrier to entry, vetting your options properly will save you from potential headaches or vehicle damage.

Look for these key indicators of a professional, high-quality mobile detailer:

1. Self-Sufficient Setup (True Mobility)

What to look for: A professional mobile unit should be completely self-contained. They should bring their own water supply, power source (generator), and lighting.   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing

The Red Flag: If a detailer asks to plug into your home's outdoor electrical outlet, run a hose from your spigot, or use your driveway lights, they are operating more like a backyard hobbyist than a professional fleet.   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing

2. General Liability & "Garage Keepers" Insurance

What to look for: Accidents can happen—a polisher can slip, a chemical can stain trim, or a tool can scratch paint. A reputable business will carry liability insurance and ideally Garage Keepers insurance (which covers your car while it is explicitly in their care). Don't hesitate to ask for proof.   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing
+ 2

The Red Flag: Hesitation, defensiveness, or a flat-out "no" when you ask if they are insured.   
Deluxe Details Mobile Services

3. Clear Processes and Professional Products

What to look for: Ask them what brands or types of products they use. Professionals use reputable, industry-standard brands (like CarPro, Gtechniq, P&S, Koch-Chemie) rather than cheap, off-the-shelf bulk products that can strip trim or damage clear coats. They should also use safe washing techniques like the two-bucket wash method, grit guards, and clean microfiber-only contact to avoid introducing swirl marks.   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing

The Red Flag: Vague answers like "we just use standard soap" or using a single dirty sponge and old bath towels for the entire vehicle.   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing

4. Transparent Pricing and Detailed Packages

What to look for: Their website or menu should clearly state what is included in each tier (e.g., specifying whether carpet extraction, clay bar treatment, or paint sealants are included). Reputable detailers will ask for photos of your car's condition or inspect it in person before giving a final quote, especially if there is heavy pet hair, mud, or stains.   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing
+ 1

The Red Flag: Extremely low, "too-good-to-be-true" pricing or vague estimates like "we'll figure out the price when we get there."   
Sabino's Famous Auto Detailing

5. Verified Reputation and a Strong Portfolio

What to look for: Look for consistent reviews across Google or Yelp rather than just a few testimonials on a Facebook page. Look at the volume of reviews (hundreds over several years signal reliable consistency) and read how they respond to any negative feedback. Additionally, check their social media or website for a portfolio of before-and-after photos of actual vehicles they’ve worked on.   
Adrian & Sons Mobile Auto Detail
+ 2

The Red Flag: A complete lack of an online footprint, stock photos instead of real work, or a pattern of complaints regarding punctuality and missed spots.   
Prked

6. Clear Satisfaction Guarantee

What to look for: A confident professional stands by their craftsmanship. Ask what their policy is if you spot a missed spot or a flaw during the final walk-through. Good detailers will happily address issues or outline a clear follow-up window.   
Deluxe Details Mobile Services
